diff.content:
diff --git a/watcher/status.py b/watcher/status.py
--- a/watcher/status.py
+++ b/watcher/status.py
@@ -1058,13 +1058,9 @@ def candidate_is_clear(checks_summary, failed_runs, failed_jobs, new_review_items):
     if not checks_summary["all_terminal"]:
         return False
-    if checks_summary["failed_count"] > 0 or checks_summary["pending_count"] > 0:
+    if checks_summary["pending_count"] > 0:
         return False
-    if int(checks_summary.get("cancelled_count") or 0) > 0:
+    if has_failed_checks(checks_summary, failed_runs, failed_jobs):
         return False
-    # Cancelled or failed workflow runs can exist while every check bucket
-    # looks terminal and green; a clear candidate requires both views clean.
-    if failed_runs or failed_jobs:
-        return False
     if new_review_items:
         return False
     return True
diff --git a/tests/test_status.py b/tests/test_status.py
--- a/tests/test_status.py
+++ b/tests/test_status.py
@@ -20,1 +20,10 @@ def test_candidate_is_clear_rejects_pending_checks():
     assert not candidate_is_clear(pending_summary(), [], [], [])
+
+
+def test_candidate_is_clear_uses_the_shared_failed_check_predicate():
+    summary = terminal_summary(cancelled_count=1)
+    assert not candidate_is_clear(summary, [], [], [])
+
+
+def test_candidate_is_clear_still_rejects_a_failed_workflow_run(monkeypatch):
+    assert not candidate_is_clear(terminal_summary(), ["run-1"], [], [])

change_contract.goal: Route the last inline copy of the failed-check policy through the shared `has_failed_checks` predicate that two other agreement sites already use.
acceptance_criteria: `candidate_is_clear` uses the shared predicate instead of its own inline conditions for cancelled and failed checks.
non_goals: Change what `has_failed_checks` itself considers a failure.
preserved_behaviors: A pending check still rejects the candidate.
A clean, fully-terminal candidate with no new review items is still accepted.

repository_instructions.label: Shared-policy rules
repository_instructions.summary: A policy predicate with more than one call site must have exactly one implementation. An inline copy at a remaining call site is a defect once the shared version exists, not a stylistic choice.

nearby_patterns.label: Two call sites already using the shared predicate

data: `has_failed_checks(checks_summary, failed_runs, failed_jobs)` already exists in `watcher/policy.py` and is already called from two other agreement sites in `watcher/reconcile.py`.
This inline copy in `candidate_is_clear` predates the shared predicate and was never migrated when the predicate was introduced.
The same duplication class previously caused two separate incidents where one call site's copy drifted from another's and produced a self-contradictory clear/not-clear result for the same candidate.
operational: `candidate_is_clear` is the gate a merge automation checks before acting, so a wrong answer here is user-visible.
